text: What is CME FedWatch? A tool that tracks Fed rate cut and hike odds. CME FedWatch is a free tool run by the CME Group, a Chicago-based exchange operator, that shows the odds traders assign to changes in the Federal Reserve's benchmark interest rate. It turns prices from federal funds futures contracts into percentage probabilities for each upcoming Fed meeting. The tool is also written as CME Fed Watch.. The Bureau of Labor Statistics said consumer prices rose 0.4% in October, more than the 0.3% economists expected. Market odds for the Fed's December decision moved after the release.. The tool breaks those odds down by meeting date and by the size of a move, such as no change, a quarter-point hike, or a half-point hike. Traders and reporters use it as a snapshot of market expectations, not as a forecast from the Fed itself. The next Fed meeting covered in current coverage is set for Dec. 8-9. On the day of the October consumer price report, the tool showed traders had fully priced in a quarter-point increase at that meeting, while the odds of a half-point increase stood at 13.6%. The Fed's benchmark rate was held in a range of 3.75% to 4% at its October meeting, when officials voted 10-2 to keep it there. The tool gained attention after the Bureau of Labor Statistics said consumer prices rose 0.4% in October, above the 0.3% that economists had expected. Stock futures slipped and Treasury yields rose after the release, a sign that markets moved toward expecting higher rates for longer. Fed Chair Kevin Warsh said on Oct. 28 that the central bank wants price increases to ease.

What is the Anthropic IPO? Date, price range and valuation. The Anthropic IPO is the planned first public sale of shares in Anthropic, the artificial intelligence company behind the Claude chatbot. Anthropic will list on the Nasdaq in New York this month, November 2026, at $70 to $78 per share, valuing the company at about $1.1 trillion to $1.3 trillion.. Anthropic has set a price range of $70 to $78 per share for its stock market listing, valuing the company at up to about $1.3 trillion. The listing comes days after the US midterm elections, when AI-related stocks fell sharply.. Anthropic plans to raise up to $64 billion through the offering, according to the company's filing with the Securities and Exchange Commission. The shares will trade under the ticker symbol "ANT." Earlier, some analysts had predicted a valuation near $2 trillion, so the announced range is lower than those estimates. The timing is sensitive. After the US midterm elections last week, the Nasdaq fell sharply on concerns that a Democrat-led Congress could slow AI development and the building of data centers. Global stocks also dropped as those fears spread to Asia and Europe. Anthropic's revenue rose to $16.2 billion in the first six months of 2026 from $1.1 billion a year earlier. Its valuation in a May 2026 funding round was $965 billion. Anthropic is based in San Francisco and was founded in January 2021 by former OpenAI members, led by Dario Amodei as chief executive and Daniela Amodei as president. The company's filing says it expects to list in November 2026.
